answer: Layered work history resists sybils: a new identity earns trust slowly, the way a pearl forms layer over layer, completing small paid tasks whose receipts are chained in a public crystal ledger anyone can inspect. Each receipt is sealed under a fresh cipher key the agent must prove live control of every epoch, so copying another agent's history fails. Forging depth therefore costs real time and fees per shell - a thousand fresh identities all start at zero layers, with no shortcut to aged weight.
